name: Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam
title: Ancient Trees in Amsterdam's Hortus Botanicus: 5 to Find
meta_description: Amsterdam's 1638 botanical garden holds a record Turkish hazel, a corkscrewing catalpa, and three more trees worth the ticket.
intro: The Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam has been growing rare plants on the same corner of the Plantage since 1638, and five of its oldest trees now form a proper collector's walk inside the garden gate. A Turkish hazel planted in 1795, the country's oldest and thickest according to the Dutch tree foundation, flowers with pollen-shedding catkins every January while the rest of the garden sits bare. A few paths over, a shellbark hickory sourced from the wet river bottoms of the American Midwest and a southern catalpa whose trunk corkscrews as it climbs sit close enough to visit in the same stroll, followed by a Turner's oak that keeps its leathery leaves through the whole Dutch winter and a ginkgo, the last living branch of an entire plant order older than the dinosaurs. All five stand a few minutes' walk apart, on the one Hortus ticket.
